newsitem.title: UK: Internet drives media mergers, more seen.
newsitem.headline: Internet drives media mergers, more seen.

text.p: A belief that the Internet will be a key to future media business boosted merger and aqcuisitions in the industry to new highs last year in Europe and North America, a report published on Tuesday showed.
The report, published by technology, media and communications industry consultant Broadview Associates, said action in 1997 would remain torrid.

Broadview said the value of mergers and acquisitions rose 33 percent to $29.3 billion in 1996, up from $22.1 billion the previous year, boosted by industry consolidation and the rapidly increasing importance of digital media.
"The advent of digital distribution, via the World Wide Web or proprietary networks, is changing the face of the information publishing, education and entertainment industries," Broadview said.
"1996 was the year many large media groups realised that the World Wide Web was here to stay, leading to some of the largest media deals to date," the report said.

Broadview cited CUC International Inc's $2 billion acquisition of Sierra On-line and Davidson & Associates in the entertainment segment, and Thomson Corp's $3.4 billion aquisition of West Publishing in information as prime examples.

Broadview said the value of deals in the digital information, entertainment and education segments soared 100 percent to $11.4 billion as companies around the world focused on CD-ROM and on-line based opportunities.
Broadview said concentration and consolidation drove European media mergers and acquisitions, where deal value was up 52 percent to $12 billion.
"We expect continued growth in 1997, with 72 percent of north American and 67 percent of European information technology firms likely to pursue mergers and acquisitions over the next 12 months."

"Almost 40 percent of media companies surveyed in north America indicate that the Internet will be one of the forces most likely to drive M&A activity in 1997, and more than half said they would pursue Internet-related M&A in the year," Broadview said.
